I'm going to be very critical about this game and it's the first time I give a negative review, but with the "overwhelmingly positive" reviews so far I reckon the game can survive a negative one. The game costs less than 10 quid, so buy it away if you know what you 're getting. I played the Prologue first so I knew what I was getting but I got it anyway because it's so cheap. The tl;dr of it is that I found the game more frustrating than entertaining, and while I keep coming back for the elegant simplicity of its design, the game punishes me with boredom instead of rewarding me with enjoyment. First, the game. You play as one of three characters. You start as "The Wanderer", and there are two more characters that have to be unlocked. So far I have unlocked one other character, "The Ronin". The two characters I've seen have different starting "tiles" (moves they can make) and different specials. The Wanderer can move through enemies, while The Ronin can push enemies back. To unlock The Ronin and the other character you have to defeat a boss for each. Defeating "The Twins" unlocks The Ronin and to unlock the third character, whose name I don't know because I haven't unlocked it, you have to defeat "Nobunaga the Wicked". I am going to go out on a limb and say that "Nobunaga the Wicked" is the final boss, but I've only reached to "The Statue", one boss after "The Twins", so I don't know. Maybe the final boss is Eren Yeager. The game loop is a turn-based fight in essentially two dimensions. Each level consists of a few squares that can be occupied by one character or enemy at a time. Movements are to the right or left only, but some moves can effectively teleport a character through multiple others, sometimes striking them in the process. Besides moving you can fire off attacks and special moves by choosing a "tile" (like a card). Tiles are placed on a Last-In-First-Out stack and the stack resolves (hint hint M:tG hint) with the press of a button, at which point all the tiles in it are executed without interruption. When you kill an enemy, they might drop some coins or potions. Potions give you temporary power ups or heal 3 HP (you start with 10). The healing point is... edamame. Wha After every fight you find a sort of idol where you can upgrade your current tiles, or two pedestals offering you one of two new tiles. You can spend coins to reroll the offerings of the idol or the pedestals. You can also spend coins in shops you find on your way through the "overland" map that takes you from fight to fight. When you die you lose all the coins, potions and tiles you had gained. Some fights are boss fights and defeating a boss gives you some number of "skulls" that you can spend to buy new tiles at the start screen. If you do, those tiles have a chance to appear on a pedestal in your next runs. You can also spend skulls to upgrade shops by adding more slots where items appear. If you die before defeating any bosses you get no skulls. The idea of a linear, turn-based fight where you can only move and strike in one dimension is simple and elegant and is what keeps me coming back for more, but the rest of the game is a chore. One big problem is that fights are very inconsistent. I don't like to whine about "the RNG" but I will have three or four runs where I fail to make it past the first boss, "Daisuke the Charger". Then I'll have one run where I'll make it three bosses later to "The Statue". I don't know what's past The Statue (OK, I suck, OK?). What's really frustrating with all that is that every time I lose, I'm taken back to the beginning and I have to do all of the same things over, and Over and OVER again. That's mind-numbingly boring, like a game of snakes and ladders. I get it, the game is a roguelike. I play Nethack, right? I die all the time in Nethack. But, in Nethack you have 13 classes (as of version 367) and a garbanzillion of items. Every time I die in Nethack and start a new game, it's a different game. Every time I die it's in a different way. In Shogun Showdun (hereafter, Sho-Sho) every time I die it's in the same way (bloody pikers), and every time I start a new game, it's the same game, with the same character, with the same tiles, with the same special, on the same map, and facing the same enemies in the same way. Even the different tiles you can find do not add much variety after all because the majority are rather narrow in scope and I find myself selecting the same few ones all the time: Swirl, Arrow, Spear and maybe once in a while a dash or a curse. So there's no variety there either. That's ===> b o r i n g <=== That boring is a direct consequence of the "elegant simplicity" of the game that I note above, so I don't know what can be done about it, and I apologise to the devs that I can't offer any more constructive criticism. I really have no idea how this game could be made more interesting. Add more starting characters? More varied tiles at the start? More diverse enemies? I mean, if I've played the game 50 times (I think I have, in 4.4 hours of play) shouldn't I get to see _something_ changing every time I start it? Despite my negative review, the game is cheap and still in early release so there's plenty of time for the devs to do better. Maybe they're focusing on stability and efficiency etc, and leaving gameplay for later, which I would say is a wise move. If you're interested in turn-based fighters, roguelikes or card games, buy it because it's an interesting take on all three. Oh, also: the graphics are cute, the music is chiptune cool and I could see no bugs. EDIT: One of the developers has replied to my review. Apparently comments can't be longer than 1000 characters, so I'm basically going to reply here. The developer, Thomas, gave a kind and patient reply! I have to say he is much better than me in dealing with negative feedback on his work (I got better; I'm a researcher, and negative feedback means my papers don't get published, which hurts a lot and not just my ego!). I thought about changing my review to "recommended" since I really don't want to hurt Sho-Sho's :) chances to be recognised and well received. I was going to do it, but I saw that the rating jumped again to "overwhelmingly positive". I think the momentary drop of the rating from my comment was the result of only having a small number of reviews, positive or negative, so far (662 at the time of writing). As more people play and review the game, the score will become normalised and, if the current trend lasts, you can expect the overall rating to be "overwhelmingly positive", certainly for "All reviews" but also for the recent ones. So don't worry about it too much. I still think Sho-Sho can survive one (and more!) negative review. I think I should leave my review as negative for the purpose of indexing it, especially for people like me who go straight to the negative reviews to figure out whether a game is for me or not. I do that a lot and I believe it has saved me a lot of frustration with games I didn't want to play after all, even if it seemed like I did at first. I think this is good not only for the player, but also for the developer: I'm guessing developers don't want players returning their game after they throw the keyboard/ controller in frustration! I hope the ceveloper can accept the possibility that my negative review not only doesn't hurt Sho-Sho's prospects, but even improves its reception a bit, by helping those who don't want to play it, avoid playing it then being grumpy about it and leaving more negative reviews. Of course there is the Prologue for that, but I'm hoping this kind of review is an extra bit of buffering between unfairly negative reviews from people who didn't have the time to finish the Prologue. OK, end of character limit for this review, also :P UPDATE: Came back after 3 years. Still grindy, but now I get more consistent runs. I killed the Shogun yay. Still only seen 1/2 of all content!

[h3]脑子：前进一步后退一步，骗他一刀，嘿嘿 手：好的，前进一步换位，硬吃伤害 脑子：打个烟雾弹，让小怪撞小怪，嘻嘻 手：好的，打个闪电 大脑：……？你没事吧？没事吧？你没事吧？[/h3] 非常有趣算术题（？）小游戏，就是经常玩动作类游戏培养出来的[strike]（非常手欠的不良）[/strike]习惯特别容易坏事导致自作孽不可活… 比如事先明明早就在脑子里把移动和伤害算的明明白白的了，可我的手在这时候就非要贪一个刚满了CD的特技（比如换位），然后就成功地实现了被前后夹击，硬吃了两刀，总之主打的就是一个自作自受。 不过游戏确实是好玩，至少在手欠之后我首先想到的是应该管管我这破手而不是卸载游戏或者重开一局（？），而且300多M的体量也没什么运行压力，就还蛮适合摸鱼时玩上一小会的。（但是要是能有撤销功能的话就更好了，哪怕有单局次数限制呢） 就我个人而言，游戏中最令我觉得惊艳的设计其实是在特技的影响下，每名角色基本上都能够为玩家提供截然不同的体验（当然，初始卡组也决定了每名角色都有着不同的起手打法与手感），也就是说，充分熟悉了某个角色并实现了通关并不意味着玩家在游戏中摸索阶段的结束。 实际上，对我来讲，它更像是一个崭新的可选的开始，因为脑子不好使如我，每次换个角色都要因为之前培养出的肌肉记忆暴毙几次，适应大半天，可以说是常做常有常学常新的游戏体验了。 （玩了浪人就再也回不去浪客了，玩了暗影就再也回不去浪人了，玩了柔术家…就再也不用转身了） 在目前的版本中，游戏共有4个可玩角色，其中： 浪客的特技是与面前一格的敌人换位（位置绝对固定的敌人除外，比如某些Boss房里的某些砍得掉的砍不掉的能加Buff能召唤小怪的雕像），非常适合拿来骗友伤，而且，浪客的初始卡组是前后攻击+弓箭，在不贪伤害的前提下也算是攻守兼备的角色了；（贪伤害：指被2血和3血的怪夹，就算能打掉一个也要硬吃一刀；守：指把对面准备冲刺的1血小怪一箭干掉） 浪人可以将敌人推至角色面对方向能够到达的最远格（位于地图边缘，或是身后没有空格的敌人不能推），很适合拿来救近战武器的急，期间若是与另一敌人发生了碰撞则是能够造成伤害，可以用来清1血冲刺小怪。另外，浪人的初始卡组是我最喜欢的2格长枪和烟雾弹（长枪在我手里：喜欢长枪；长枪在敌人手里：给我死！），既能打伤害，又有保命手段；（靠烟雾弹换位骗伤害简直太好用了…给烟雾弹升不占回合再把冷却尽可能拉到最低在我这基本上等于版本答案） 暗影每次移动都是移动至可移动的最远格（脚底巨滑，这很冰面谜题），并且可以穿过敌人（浪客，但不影响敌人位置），但敌人位于两端或身后没有空格时不能穿[strike]（这时候难道不应该沿用跳棋规则吗！）[/strike]。初始卡组是飞爪和前后攻击（可以对着那个抓你过来再砍一刀的小怪抓过来再砍一刀报仇了！），只要不被夹击，就可以机动性很强； 而柔术家可以将身后的敌人丢至面对方向的最远处（浪人，但不用转身），初始卡组是击退拳（效果类似浪人的特技，但可以通过升级附加各种属性，甚至可以出牌不占回合数）和对全部非满血敌人造成伤害。（乍一看真挺厉害，但想要实现用它一张卡卷死一屏敌人细想想其实还怪麻烦的…） [b]总之，非常期待未来能够加入更多的角色啦。[/b] （看了眼roadmap，未来还会加入两名角色和两张大地图，建议早买早享受） 不过喜欢归喜欢，目前版本的游戏还是有着一些缺点的。 比如受单周目流程长度的限制，玩家能够顺利拿到想要的卡牌使卡组成型的概率会随着卡池的逐渐扩充而逐渐降低（因为能选卡的事件确实不算多），要么运气爆发杀杀杀爽，要么战战兢兢如履薄冰，既打不出伤害，又得想方设法躲开小怪们的连续迫害，实际上就还蛮看脸的，是非常坏文明（超大声）。（所以浪人是我用得最多的角色，因为自带烟雾弹，就算没能成型，容错率也会高一些） 虽然确实可以靠刷新来实现目的，但这游戏赚钱实际上还蛮艰难的（真有人敢把血卖空就为了赚钱吗），至少我是更愿意留着钱拿去商店用，换取更稳定的角色强化，而不是赌上全部身家成功地把CD-2刷成CD-1。（痛，太痛了） [code]欢迎参观我的： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/7421824]双鱼星✪ω✪皇家飛机场[/url] 如果你喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到。[/code]

游戏很好玩，很有创意，我给你差评是想作者看到你做游戏没做完的两个大点，这两个大点已经能气的玩家砸键盘了。 1、键鼠玩家应该都这样，在你深思熟虑之后想要长按鼠标来滑动更改行动卡牌的位置时，离奇的给你把卡牌撤销了，于是你又长按拖动后又耗费了体力，而当你重新拖动上去后尝试在更改位置，又踏马开始撤销.......想象一下如果此时正在敲boss你该有多炸裂。你这位置判定区域是给人玩的？？？？？？ 2、这一点依旧恶心人，100金币一直刷新出来等级上限不说，你的“加一伤害，加一冷却”这个词条是在我花完几十金币后出来恶心我的，而我的第一个词条是加一伤害，所以我请问你的一正一负的词条做出来有屌用？你要么就改成加二减二，请然我感觉攒了半天的金币花的不冤。

663h终于全成就。 作为肉鸽，为了做特殊成就，有刷的要素，但更多的是战斗中的思考。 是少数的能让我进入心流的游戏，体验过生死一线的绞尽脑汁，也有过为了速杀不惜卖血。一路走来，甚至感受到了自己的成长，从最初对敌人的理解到后面对天赋，不同角色特性，行动块，乃至整个流程，在实践中加深认识，用在下一场战斗，嗯，很爽。

爽局无聊，屎局折磨，在大量的折磨局中找到了少量的正常局。 玩家控制的角色移动一步，怪物也移动一步，怪物数量比主角多，所以给予玩家技能和可以升级的武器来弥补不平衡，但是随着游戏的进展，开始堆怪，并且有远程有近战，每个波次刷新也无法判断位置，怪的属性和技能也得到增强，怪物的提升远大于正常局玩家的提升。想要解锁强力武器和技能，就要同时解锁大量孱弱的武器和技能来污染池子，刷新池子的费用过高，roll不出合适的武器和技能，这一局游戏就开始变得折磨。 我认为这个游戏的设计初衷可能就是鼓励玩家反复重开roll种，而不是局内的运营。路线和事件过于固定和死板，给的金钱也浮动不大，想在战斗后刷新找提升就意味着商店空过，但是在商店如果没有需要的技能，提升也微乎其微，充斥着看脸和运气，玩家主观能动性的作用很小。 打小怪的难度远大于打boss，尤其是在很小的区域每个回合都来新的一波的连战，如果输出的频率和伤害跟不上，基本上就可以宣告失败了，其实跟上了也不一定能过，每一波的刷怪位置也较为随机，这就出现所谓的必吃伤害的局面，很多人把这个游戏类比于下棋，我认为也挺像的，这种刷怪像下棋时对面直接把棋子摆在棋盘上将军，就是必杀的阵型，完全是在耍赖，玩起来很憋屈，棋盘至少是二维，这个游戏却是在一条线上，就更容易出现这种情况。游戏对每一步进行即时存档，无法sl来找最优解避免战损。 重复度很高加上很吃运气的一款小游戏，不太适合喜欢在肉鸽的每一局尽力运营的玩家，挫败感还是蛮强的，可能更适合习惯重开roll种的玩家，能得到更好的体验。
无聊，一个运气远远比策略更重要的策略游戏。

[h1]《将军对决》非常符合我心目中对一款优秀的roguelike游戏的定义。[/h1] 游戏机制本身非常简单，上手门槛只需要你精通个位数加减法，下棋一般走一步想三步的玩法意料之外的上头。点睛之笔在于巧妙地利用了意图系统，让操纵的角色可以用技能和走位使得敌人互相攻击，每一次如同太极一般的借力打力让对手自相残杀都会给玩家带来巨大的成就感。 局外成长是单纯为了将游戏在一开始的复杂程度控制在一个合理的范围内，让玩家循序渐进地接触并理解新的招式。敌人的行动逻辑也非常容易观察出来，基本上打过几次次就明白这个敌人会如何行动，大概如何应对。这两点和杀戮尖塔的设计理念完全一致，也是我最喜欢和欣赏的设计。 如果你需要一个闲暇时稍微动动脑筋的高质量小游戏，这将是一个极好的选择。

Build a deck to defeat the Shogun and his henchmen in this addictive roguelike with turn-based combat and tons of unlocks. Simple pixel art, but mindblowing strategic gameplay.
Shogun Showdown is a challenging and hard to put down. The tactical scenarios are enthralling since even with a less-than-desirable hand of cards, it is possible to overcome with cunning.

Turn-based combat where every action counts. Carefully position yourself, build up and unleash your attacks at the right time. Gain new skills and build the best deck you can before facing the Shogun.
Screen shake can be disabled.
So, whether we call it a turn-based deck-builder or a turn-based RPG, all that really matters is if Shogun Showdown is any fun. It most definitely is. Shogun Showdown is a total blast.
